dimensions.note: The model holds no credentials. The Jev key is read by @swamp/typesafe-ai from the vault, the Capture instance needs no key, and @webframp/github uses the user's gh login. Issue #49 removes every recipe, pack and sync code path from this package: running recipes and pulling packs now happen in @puddleworks/recipes, which has its own review. The only subprocess left is search: `swamp` on the PATH as an argv array, with at most four words matching [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*. load still withholds a turn that looks like it holds a secret: the stored text is a placeholder and Jev, match, search and raise are skipped (tested). The workflow's confirm step does take the cleaned turn text, as match does: a withheld turn reaches it as the placeholder, which is not a yes, so it only drops a plan. The hook validates session_id against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$ before it becomes an input, because swamp reads a value starting with @ as a file (tested). The turn itself still travels by file path, never as an input. Issues #52 and #53: Issues #52 and #53 add no credentials. A withheld turn is never tested against alwaysLlm or match, so a secret-looking turn reaches neither. Issue #42: raise now also passes the cleaned turn as phrase and the candidates' names. The phrase is the text the description already carried, so nothing new leaves the repo; a withheld turn never reaches search, so a secret-looking turn is never a phrase. A capture: turn has no phrase.

load, recall, merged, search and reply log at info on entry and completion with structured placeholders. search logs its query (up to four content words of a deterministic turn), as the match step did before; a withheld turn never reaches search. A bad puddlerouter.yaml entry logs at info as before. The turn text is not logged. Failures in confirm, match and execute are logged by @puddleworks/recipes and swamp. Issues #52 and #53: alwaysLlm logs the matching pattern, or none, and any config errors. It logs the owner's pattern, never the turn. Issue #42: No new log lines; the phrase is not logged.

Every recipe step has allowFailure: a failed confirm, match or execute leaves its outputs absent, and the has() guards pass the turn on. A missing recipes instance was checked live: the hook passes and search still runs. reply handles each outcome: ran ok blocks with the answer, ran and failed hints Claude to tell the user and not to rerun (it may have made some changes), refused hints that nothing changed, ask and would-ask block or record the plan (each tested). A failed search gives kind none and is not cached. parseConfig never throws: invalid YAML or a bad allow entry is dropped and reported. The hook fails open on any error or timeout, and the day stamp means a failed sync waits for the next day (documented). A timed-out turn or a failed confirm can leave a plan until the next turn or its 10-minute expiry: the plan can then only run on a bare yes in that session, within the expiry. Issues #52 and #53: alwaysLlm has allowFailure and every read is guarded by has(), so a failed check routes as today. A bad pattern or a non-list value goes into config errors, is logged, and the other entries still load. A failed match carries on to route; tested in the workflow tests and run live. Issue #42: Capture refuses a phrase over 500 characters, so a longer turn gets a blank phrase and is still logged with the turn in its description (tested at 500 and 501). raise keeps allowFailure, so a refused request still passes as no request logged.

make test: 125 unit tests and 84 hook and workflow tests pass. New or rewritten: searchTurn and captureSearch, the search method, every reply outcome for confirm and execute, the guards on merged, route, decide, match, search and execute after a confirm, the session id's shape, the skipped-turn plan drop, and the sync starting after the workflow on a routed turn, including when the workflow fails. version_test.ts pins model version to manifest and upgrades. Live, through the real hook in a worktree: no index then a pack recipe answering via reads:, plan then yes, a second yes, no thanks, /review then yes, shadow, no session, no recipes instance. See docs/puddlerouter.md, Live check. Issues #52 and #53: make test: 145 unit tests and 90 hook and workflow tests pass. New: config parsing of alwaysLlm, alwaysLlmHit, every reply outcome for alwaysLlm and a recipe with no route, the guards on match, route, decide, search and merged, the hook note, and the example file. Six real shadow workflow runs are in docs/puddlerouter.md. Not run live: a miss followed by a real Jev answer, because the worktree has no Jev key. Issue #42: make test: 148 unit tests and 90 hook and workflow tests pass. New: the phrase is the turn unchanged across lines and past the 80-character title, blank over 500 characters, candidates in c1..c3 order and empty with no content words, captureSearch has none, and raise wires phrase and candidateExtensions. swamp workflow validate passes, raise's inputs included, against capture-log-request 2026.11.04.1. capture-log-request run in a scratch repo with a two-line phrase and two candidate names succeeded: the request holds the phrase as its requested phrase and its recipe starts with that phrase and both names. Not run: the whole router workflow live.

Each method writes one fixed-name resource as a new version. The Capture request is keyed by the turn's sourceRef, so a repeated turn gets the same request. A plan runs once: @puddleworks/recipes marks it used before running, and a second yes was checked live to route as normal. Starting the daily sync from the exit trap stops it holding the recipes lock during the turn; a turn typed straight after it can still time out and fail open, about once a day at most (documented). Route and search cache entries are deterministic functions of the turn, so rewriting is harmless. Issues #52 and #53: alwaysLlm writes one fixed-name resource as a new version and changes nothing else. Moving match ahead of route adds no writes: a recipe that makes changes still asks first, and a turn with a recipe match skips the recall cache, so it neither reads nor writes a route. Issue #42: The key is still the turn's sourceRef; Capture records the phrase only when it first creates the request, so a repeat returns the same request.

Depends on @puddleworks/recipes methods match, execute and confirm, reading only the fields its README lists: matched, recipeId, captures; action, ok, text, error, recipeId. Every read is guarded by has(). Tests and the live run cover those fields against version 2026.11.04.2 of the type. The other contracts are unchanged: @swamp/git and @webframp/github in merged, @swamp/typesafe-ai for Jev, @puddleworks/capture-log-request for raise. The manifest lists @puddleworks/recipes. It is on the beta channel; whether pulling this package brings a beta-only dependency is not documented, so the README's desk steps pull it explicitly first. Issues #52 and #53: The manifest pin moves to @puddleworks/recipes 2026.11.05.1, whose patterns must match the whole turn and refuse catch-alls. That guarantee is what makes running match before route safe. reply still reads only the same match and execute fields, and reports a recipe turn as deterministic with no confidence rather than 0. Issue #42: capture-log-request takes phrase (string, at most 500, default blank) and candidateExtensions (strings of at most 200, at most 50) from @puddleworks/capture 2026.11.04.1, checked against Capture's source. The router sends at most three names. The pin moves from 2026.10.28.2 to 2026.11.04.1 (upstream_extensions.json and the capture and viewer instances' typeVersion).

load reads the turn file and holds no handle. The hook's exit trap removes the turn and output files on every way out, including failures (tested through the existing cleanup checks). The sync started in the trap has its streams redirected, so the hook doesn't wait for it (tested: under 2 s while the fake sync hangs). Deno.Command in search has stdin null and collects its pipes. Issues #52 and #53: alwaysLlm reads puddlerouter.yaml through the existing loadConfig and holds no handle. Patterns come only from the owner's local file; a slow pattern is bounded by the hook's timeout, which fails open. Issue #42: No new handles or files.

Plain z.object schemas with enums and iso datetimes, no passthrough. SearchSchema and the new reply arguments are the same kind; resultAction and confirmAction are plain strings because a newer recipes version could add an action, and buildReply treats an unknown action as no answer. Issues #52 and #53: AlwaysLlmSchema and AlwaysLlmArgsSchema are plain z.object schemas with no passthrough; the reply argument is an optional boolean. Issue #42: SearchSchema gains requestPhrase (string) and requestCandidates (array of strings), plain z.object fields with no passthrough.

turn, reply, recall, search and merged: 14d, garbageCollection 2000. routeCache 7d and searchCache 1d, garbageCollection 1, since only the latest is read. The removed specs (match, result, resultCache, recipeIndex) are not read by anything here; their old data ages out under swamp's own rules. Issues #52 and #53: The new alwaysLlm resource has lifetime 14d and garbageCollection 2000, the same as turn, reply, recall, search and merged. Issue #42: No new resources; search keeps 14d and garbageCollection 2000.
Not a lifecycle model; stateless per-turn methods plus caches that expire.

This package makes no change itself beyond swamp data and raise's existing Capture request (live mode only). A recipe that makes changes runs only after @puddleworks/recipes has shown a plan and had a bare yes in the same session within 10 minutes. The router's part is to send only the next typed turn to confirm, and to have a skipped typed turn drop the plan in the background (tested and checked live). reads: is the owner's own decision in their own file: only exact methods, no wildcards, and packs can't set it. Issues #52 and #53: Running match earlier changes no safety rule: a recipe that makes changes still shows a plan and waits for a bare yes, and a listed phrase is never taken as that yes. An alwaysLlm turn runs nothing and logs nothing in Capture, because search is skipped and raise needs search's output. Issue #42: No new action: raise still runs only in live mode for a turn nothing can answer, or a capture: turn.

Mechanical check: load writes turn/turn, recall recall/recall, search search/search, reply reply/reply, merged merged/merged; caches use route-v1- and search- prefixes, so no two specs share a name. Every SearchSchema field (kind, query, candidates, criteria, requestTitle, requestDescription, requestKey, searchedAt) is written by both searchTurn and captureSearch. Issues #52 and #53: alwaysLlm writes alwaysLlm/alwaysLlm, so no two specs share a name. Every AlwaysLlmSchema field (matched, pattern, checkedAt) is written. Issue #42: Mechanical check: both searchTurn and captureSearch write every SearchSchema field, including requestPhrase and requestCandidates.

recall and search read their cache entries with context.readResource only and parse with zod. The workflow passes recipe results to reply as inputs, so the model reads no other model's data. Issues #52 and #53: alwaysLlm reads only its own repo's local config file; the workflow passes its result to reply as an input. Issue #42: Unchanged: raise reads search's outputs through steps.

Stored turn and reply data are rewritten each turn and never read across versions. Issues #52 and #53: Model version goes from 2026.11.04.1 to 2026.11.05.1 with one upgrades entry that leaves global arguments alone, pinned by version_test.ts. The instance YAML's typeVersion matches, and so does the recipes instance's against upstream_extensions.json. Issue #42: Model version goes from 2026.11.05.1 to 2026.11.09.1 with one upgrades entry that leaves global arguments alone, pinned by version_test.ts. The instance YAML's typeVersion matches.
